steps.text: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C). Coat a 10-inch pie plate with cooking spray.
Combine zucchini, tomato, onion, and Parmesan cheese in the prepared pie plate.
Beat baking mix, eggs, milk, salt, and black pepper together in a bowl until smooth; pour over zucchini mixture.
Bake in the preheated oven until a knife inserted into center comes out clean, about 30 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Zucchini Tomato Pie
raw_recipe.description: Zucchini, tomato, and onion combine with Parmesan cheese and baking mix, like Bisquick, to make this pie recipe a snap to throw together on a summer day.
raw_recipe.name: Zucchini Tomato Pie

review.reviewBody:
As written, definayely four - with a few minor changes 5+++!

I sauteed the onion until deep golden brown, (we LOVELOVELOVE carmelized onions) plus sauteed the zucchini a little - it's crunchy otherwise. I also added more cheese than was called for.
The "impossible pies" from the back of the box call for 2/3 c mix, 3/4 c milk and 2 eggs - so that's the topping that I used.
I've made this 1000 times with 1000 different fillings - any cheese wotrks, most any veggie in most any combo. It's also good with chopped cooked meats! This is a terrific basic "starter". Thanks!

I followed the other suggestions and ramped up the flavor with Italian herbs and garlic. I increased the parmesan cheese and made it a meal with protein by pre-cooking in a skillet, 1/2 italian ground sausage and 1/2 lean hamburger. I sauteed the onions until carmelized and also cooked the zucchini and tomatoes separately in skillets and drained well befre mixing. I also had some pizza dough on hand so I weaved a top crust to give it some crunch and add to the presentation.

I followed Robbin818 suggestions to sauté the veggies and adjust the bisquick recipe and then seasoned the veggies with salt, pepper and seasoning before putting them in the pie pan. I also added a little Parmesan cheese to the bisquick mix. It’s amazing! I won’t be having trouble using up the zucchini this summer!

This was not earth-shattering, but very good!! I'll make this again. I used the "easy biscuit mixture" recipe on this site for the baking mix. I sauteed the zucchini (of which I used about a cup extra) and onion prior to cooking with about a clove's worth of minced garlic. I also combined everything in a bowl, plus parsley and paprika, before putting it in the pan so the veggies would be mixed well. It turned out great!

5 stars - we added 1/2 c shred Monterrey jack in addition to the Parmesan cheese; 4oz sliced can mushrooms. Red onion. Tossed in some dry spices: garlic powder and onion powder. Pouring the egg / milk mixture caused it to run over the top so I dumped the whole think in a bowl, mixed lightly and then poured back into the pie tin. Sprinkled with dry parsley & S&P. We are at high altitude and had to cook it an additional 7-8 minutes to cook the middle fully. *** not strong flavors, so it complimented entree well.

This was so good! Made a great brunch item. I sautéed the veggies first to cook out some of the water, added a clove of crushed garlic and some bell pepper. I also used a bit less of the baking mix and eggs - 1/2 c each of baking mix and milk, and 2 eggs. You do have to let it sit 5-10 mins to help it firm up.

I followed the recipe ingredients, but I sauted the vegetables first, as suggested by other reviewers. It turned out OK, but I wouldn't make it again. For my taste, there were not enough vegetables in the recipes for the amount of the breading. I might consider doubling the vegetables and adding additional spices, but wouldn't recommend the recipe as written.

As with other reviewers, I fried the onions and zucchini and tomatoes before putting into the pie. I have sourdough for biscuits that I am always looking for recipes to use and they turned out perfectly instead of using the recipe contained herein for the biscuit topping. Everything else was as written. I will definitely make again to use up both zucchini and tomatoes.

Sautéed zucchini, onions, garlic and carrots. Added shrimp and tomatoes. Put the bisquick mixture over the top (in the same skillet) and popped it in the oven. Realized I forgot the cheese, so added it to the top in the last ten minutes. Yummy! We ate the entire thing!!!

Used fresh veggies from my garden. Also added some fresh herbs for flavor. Didn't have biscuit mix so made my own. I should have cooked a little longer at a lower temperature since I use a convection oven.

With some modifications, this recipe is easily 5 stars. I saute the zucchini and onion until slightly browned. This makes the veggies not as crunchy, which is what I prefer in this dish. I also add more seasoning: I sprinkle the top with Italian seasoning, pepper, and a little salt. I use the Bisquick box recipe for the dough portion. I also sometimes make a double batch and put it in a 13x9 pan and cook it until it's golden brown on top. Great to take to work for lunch throughout the week!
Great base recipe, easy to tweak with what you have. I added greek yogurt instead of milk, mozzarella instead of parm and put dollops of ricotta. Delicious way to use up garden veggies.
A great dinner. My wife says I can make it often! Yummy!
Leave out the bisquick and it’s a five star.

I added colby jack and Italian blend shredded cheeses which included Parmesan but even tho it looked pretty and delicious, it was actually bland. And I used a 5 pepper and 5 salt seasoning blend instead of just salt and pepper as on recipe. I may try again with more seasoning. Probably garlic also.
I was looking for a recipe to help use up some of my end-of-the-garden veggies, and this one worked perfectly. My husband liked it too. I will make it again.
Delicious
Very good. I made it 3 times in 3 days. Everyone wanted more
My recipe was too big for a 10 inch pie pan so I increased amounts and added a 11 inch pan along with it! Added triple the cheese.
Awesome dish and easy to make. Did use a seasoned salt. Would make again!
